summary.headline: Proceed, but only with targeted diligence conditions
summary.overview: Alpine IT is a profitable, growing MSP (TTM revenue ~$2.41M; EBITDA ~$824.8K; ~51% gross margin) and appears bankable for an SBA loan at the 3.0x SDE base case. However, three deal-killers remain unresolved: an unexplained ~ $200K SDE reconciliation gap, missing federal/state tax filings, and material owner key-person dependency (owner is the lead engineer and primary client contact, with a market replacement cost ~ $120K/yr). Recommendation: conditional buy only after targeted diligence (tax returns, SDE support, client contract verification) and transaction structure (escrow/earnout + employment/transition agreement) to mitigate the two financial and one operational impediment. Financing is feasible, but lenders will require conservative underwriting and contractual protections tied to the unresolved items.

keyFindings.title: Owner is primary technical resource — material replacement cost
keyFindings.description: Owner performs lead engineering and technical-director duties; the SDE schedule deducts a market-rate Tech Director of -$120K, indicating recurring replacement cost and concentrated operational risk if owner departs.

keyFindings.title: Unexplained SDE reconciliation gap (~$200k)
keyFindings.description: Reported SDE ($564.5K) does not reconcile with EBITDA ($824.8K) and the disclosed add-backs/subtractions, leaving ~ $200K unexplained. This gap directly affects valuation, debt sizing, and buyer cash needs.

keyFindings.title: Missing state filings / potential nexus exposure
keyFindings.description: No state tax filings were provided; if the company has multi-state activity there may be unfiled returns, penalties, or interest that could create post-close liabilities.

keyFindings.title: Missing federal tax returns and multi-year financials
keyFindings.description: Seller did not provide federal tax returns or full multi-year financial statements. Without tax returns/bank records, revenue, deductions, and historical earnings cannot be verified—exposes buyer to tax liabilities and SDE misstatement risk.

keyFindings.title: Owner key-person dependency
keyFindings.description: Owner acts as lead engineer and technical director. Departure (relocation to PNW) creates immediate operational gap requiring $120K/yr replacement at market rate. All client relationships run through owner.

Require a seller-provided SDE / EBITDA reconciliation signed by the seller and a CPA, plus a $200K escrow/true-up tied to tax/financial verification.

Structure part of the purchase price as seller financing or earnout (12–24 months) tied to recurring revenue/EBITDA retention and require a holdback for tax/state filing liabilities.

buyerFacingDimensions.label: Financial Quality
buyerFacingDimensions.summary: Alpine IT: $2.41M TTM revenue, ~51% gross margin, $824.8k EBITDA (~34% margin) with strong working capital (≈$361k) and no long-term debt on the balance sheet. Primary concerns: an unexplained ≈$200k SDE reconciliation gap and material owner-dependent technical functions (replacement ≈$120k) — resolve before relying on reported SDE for financing. Review incomplete: no financial statements or federal/state tax returns were provided, preventing verification of revenue or deductions. Primary risks are missing returns/state filings and unknown entity classification; obtain missing returns, bank records, 1099s, and state filings for a definitive assessment.

buyerFacingDimensions.label: Revenue Durability
buyerFacingDimensions.summary: AR portfolio is healthy: $148.6K total, 93.1% current, zero balances beyond 90 days, DSO ~23 days (report notes ~14 days). Concentration is the primary concern—top 5 customers represent 54.4% of AR, with Apex Financial Group alone at 16.6%. Only $800 sits in the 61-90 day bucket (18 miscellaneous accounts) and $9,400 in 31-60 days (Green Valley Medical Clinic $3K + others $6.4K). Write-off risk is minimal at $800 (0.5% of AR). No critical or high-severity collection issues. Alpine IT Solutions operates in a growing MSP/cybersecurity industry with strong tailwinds (regulatory compliance demand, cloud migration). Denver metro offers expanding SMB demand but high competitor density. The business has attractive fundamentals: 67% recurring revenue, 94% client retention, 34% EBITDA margin, zero debt, and 10%+ annual growth. Key risks are owner key-person dependency (high severity — owner is lead engineer and primary client relationship), 18% MRR concentration in a single client (Apex Financial), and talent retention during transition. Macro headwinds (elevated interest rates, IT labor cost inflation) are partially offset by strong regulatory demand drivers. Overall market conditions are favorable for a well-managed acquisition, but transition execution risk is material.

buyerFacingDimensions.label: Bankability
buyerFacingDimensions.summary: Bankable for a first-time buyer under SBA 7(a) at the 3.0x SDE base case (asking $1,693,500): DSCR 2.57 (well above 1.25), SBA eligibility confirmed. Buyer needs ~$527k cash at close (incl. $338.7k down) and should expect post-close liquidity (~$100k).
